# 7-Zip

7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio.

## About

7-Zip is free software that provides:
- High compression ratio using the LZMA and LZMA2 compression algorithms
- Support for multiple archive formats (7z, ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, TAR, and others)
- Strong AES-256 encryption in 7z and ZIP formats
- Self-extracting capability for 7z format
- Integration with Windows Shell
- Powerful command-line interface
- Plugin support for file managers

## Website

Official website: [7-zip.org](https://7-zip.org)

## License

7-Zip is distributed under the GNU LGPL license (with some components under other open-source licenses).
See the DOC directory for detailed license information.

## Supported Formats

**Packing / unpacking**: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM

**Unpacking only**: APFS, AR, ARJ, CAB, CHM, CPIO, CramFS, DMG, EXT, FAT, GPT, HFS, IHEX, ISO, LZH, LZMA, MBR, MSI, NSIS, NTFS, QCOW2, RAR, RPM, SquashFS, UDF, UEFI, VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, XAR and Z.

For more information, visit the official 7-Zip website.

7-Zip 26.00 Sources
-------------------

7-Zip is a file archiver for Windows.

7-Zip Copyright (C) 1999-2026 Igor Pavlov.


License Info
------------

7-Zip is free software distributed under the GNU LGPL
(except for unRar code). Also some  code
is licensed under the "BSD 3-clause License".
Read "License.txt" for more infomation about license.

Notes about unRAR license:

Please check main restriction from unRar license:

   2. The unRAR sources may be used in any software to handle RAR
      archives without limitations free of charge, but cannot be used
      to re-create the RAR compression algorithm, which is proprietary.
      Distribution of modified unRAR sources in separate form or as a
      part of other software is permitted, provided that it is clearly
      stated in the documentation and source comments that the code may
      not be used to develop a RAR (WinRAR) compatible archiver.

In brief it means:
1) You can compile and use compiled files under GNU LGPL rules, since
   unRAR license almost has no restrictions for compiled files.
   You can link these compiled files to LGPL programs.
2) You can fix bugs in source code and use compiled fixed version.
3) You can not use unRAR sources to re-create the RAR compression algorithm.


LZMA SDK
--------

This package also contains some files from LZMA SDK
You can download LZMA SDK from:
  http://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
LZMA SDK is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov.


How to compile in Windows
-------------------------

To compile the sources to Windows binaries you need Visual Studio compiler and/or Windows SDK.
You can use latest Windows Studio 2017/2019/2022 to compile binaries for x86, x64, arm64 and arm platforms.
Also you can use old compilers for some platforms:
  x86   : Visual C++ 6.0 with Platform SDK
  x64   : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  ia64 (itanium)  : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  arm for Windows CE : Standard SDK for Windows CE 5.0

If you use MSVC6, specify also Platform SDK directories at top of directories lists:
Tools / Options / Directories
  - Include files
  - Library files

Also you need Microsoft Macro Assembler:
  - ml.exe for x86
  - ml64.exe for x64
You can use ml.exe from Windows SDK for Windows Vista or some later versions.

There are two ways to compile 7-Zip binaries:
1) via makefile in command line.
2) via dsp file in Visual Studio.

The dsp file compiling can be used for development and debug purposes.
All final 7-Zip binaries are compiled via makefiles, that provide best
optimization options.


How to compile with makefile in Windows
---------------------------------------

Some macronames can be defined for compiling with makefile:

PLATFORM
  with possible values: x64, x86, arm64, arm, ia64

OLD_COMPILER
  for old VC compiler, like MSCV 6.0.

MY_DYNAMIC_LINK
  for dynamic linking to the run-time library (msvcrt.dll).
  The default makefile option is static linking to the run-time library.

To compile all 7-Zip files for x64 with Visual Studio 2022,
use the following command sequence:

  cd SRC\CPP\7zip
  %comspec% /k "C:\Program Files\VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
  nmake

You can use another "vcvars*.bat" files from "VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build" directory
to compile for other platforms:
  vcvars64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_arm64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_x86.bat

Also you can compile single binary from directory with related project.
For example, to compile 7za.exe, use the following command sequence:
  cd SRC\CPP\7zip\Bundles\Alone\
  nmake


Compiling 7-Zip for Unix/Linux
------------------------------

There are several options to compile 7-Zip with different compilers: gcc and clang.
Also 7-Zip code contains two versions for some parts of code: in C and in Assembeler.
So if you compile the version with Assembeler code, you will get faster 7-Zip binary.

7-Zip's assembler code uses the following syntax for different platforms:

1) x86 and x86-64 (AMD64): MASM syntax.
   Now there are 3 programs that supports MASM syntax in Linux.
'    'Asmc Macro Assembler, JWasm, and UASM. Note that JWasm now doesn't support some
      cpu instructions used in 7-Zip.
   So you must install Asmc Macro Assembler in Linux or UASM, if you want to compile
   fastest version of 7-Zip  x86 and x86-64:
     https://github.com/nidud/asmc
     https://github.com/Terraspace/UASM


2) arm64: GNU assembler for ARM64 with preprocessor.
   That systax is supported by GCC and CLANG for ARM64.

There are different binaries that can be compiled from 7-Zip source.
There are 2 main files in folder for compiling:
  makefile        - that can be used for compiling Windows version of 7-Zip with nmake command
  makefile.gcc    - that can be used for compiling Linux/macOS versions of 7-Zip or Windows version
                    with MINGW (GCC) with make command.
                   
At first you must change the current folder to folder that contains `makefile.gcc`:

  cd CPP/7zip/Bundles/Alone2

import zlib
data=open('/tmp/t3/a.txt','rb').read()+b''+open('/tmp/t3/sub/b.txt','rb').read()
print("%08X"%(zlib.crc32(data)&0xffffffff))
# Maybe aggregate is hashing the individual hash values? Or incremental with something between?
# For folder case single file but names hash 8D032907-00000001 . Data and names: hashing name bytes + data? order?
# Try possibilities for sub case: files: sub/ folder, sub/b.txt
candidates={}
d=open('/tmp/t3/sub/b.txt','rb').read()
for encoding in ['utf-8','utf-16le','utf-16be']:
  for name in ['sub/','sub/b.txt','sub','sub/b.txt\n']:
    candidates[f"{encoding} name+data {name!r}"]= name.encode(encoding)+d
    candidates[f"{encoding} data+name {name!r}"]= d+name.encode(encoding)
    # both names
  candidates[f"{encoding} bothnames+data"]= 'sub/'.encode(encoding)+'sub/b.txt'.encode(encoding)+d
  candidates[f"{encoding} interleaved"]= 'sub/'.encode(encoding)+'sub/b.txt'.encode(encoding)+d
for k,v in candidates.items(): print(k,"%08X"%(zlib.crc32(v)&0xffffffff))

PY"}

def make_table(poly):
    tab=[]
    for i in range(256):

import sys,os,shutil,time
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from probe import show
d='/tmp/tupd'
if os.path.exists(d): shutil.rmtree(d)
os.makedirs(d); os.chdir(d)
open('a.txt','w').write('A1\n'); open('b.txt','w').write('B1\n'); open('c.txt','w').write('C1\n')
for f in ['a.txt','b.txt','c.txt']: os.utime(f,(1000000000,1000000000))
show(['a','u.7z','a.txt','b.txt','c.txt'])
show(['a','u.zip','a.txt','b.txt','c.txt'])
# modify b newer
open('b.txt','w').write('B2 longer\n'); os.utime('b.txt',(1100000000,1100000000))
show(['a','u.7z','b.txt']); show(['l','u.7z'])

open('b.txt','w').write('B3 even longer content\n'); os.utime('b.txt',(900000000,900000000))
show(['a','u.7z','b.txt']); show(['l','u.7z'])
show(['u','u.7z','b.txt']); show(['l','u.7z'])
# u with newer
open('b.txt','w').write('B4\n'); os.utime('b.txt',(1200000000,1200000000))
show(['u','u.7z','b.txt']); show(['l','u.7z'])
# u new file

show(['rn','u.7z','nosuch','x'])
# delete wildcard
show(['d','u.7z','*.txt']); show(['l','u.7z'])
PY

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY' > /tmp/log_open.txt 2>&1
import sys,os,shutil
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from probe import show,run
d='/tmp/topen'
if os.path.exists(d): shutil.rmtree(d)
os.makedirs(d); os.chdir(d)
open('text.txt','w').write('just text\n')
open('empty.7z','wb').write(b'')
open('fake.7z','wb').write(b'not a 7z archive at all 1234567890')
open('fake.zip','wb').write(b'PK\x03\x04 garbage')
open('rand.bin','wb').write(os.urandom(100))
# zero file with no ext
open('zero','wb').write(b'')
for f in ['text.txt','empty.7z','fake.7z','fake.zip','rand.bin','zero']:
    for cmd in ['l','t','x']:
        extra=['-y'] if cmd=='x' else []
        show([cmd]+extra+[f])
# truncated valid
import subprocess
show(['a','good.7z','text.txt'])
data=open('good.7z','rb').read()
for n in [10,32,40,len(data)-10,len(data)-1]:
    open(f'trunc{n}.7z','wb').write(data[:n]); show(['l',f'trunc{n}.7z']); show(['t',f'trunc{n}.7z'])
# corrupted packed byte
bad=bytearray(data); bad[40]^=0xff; open('corrupt.7z','wb').write(bytes(bad))
show(['l','corrupt.7z']); show(['t','corrupt.7z']); show(['x','-y','corrupt.7z','-ooutc'])
# corrupted header crc byte near end
bad2=bytearray(data); bad2[-5]^=0xff; open('corrupt2.7z','wb').write(bytes(bad2))
show(['l','corrupt2.7z']); show(['t','corrupt2.7z'])
PY
cat /tmp/log_open.txt"}

python3 -u - << 'PY' > /tmp/log_methods.txt 2>&1
import sys,os,shutil
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from probe import show
d='/tmp/tmeth'
if os.path.exists(d): shutil.rmtree(d)
os.makedirs(d); os.chdir(d)
open('f.txt','w').write('hello compressible world\n'*200)
open('raw.bin','wb').write(bytes(range(256))*20)
methods=['Copy','LZMA','LZMA2','BZip2','Deflate','PPMd','Delta','BCJ','LZMA2:dict=1m','BADM']
for m in methods:
    show(['a',f'-m0={m}','o.7z','f.txt'])
    if os.path.exists('o.7z'): show(['l','-slt','o.7z']); os.remove('o.7z')
# filters chains
show(['a','-m0=BCJ','-m1=LZMA2','o.7z','raw.bin']); show(['l','-slt','o.7z'])
os.remove('o.7z')
show(['a','-mx0','o.7z','f.txt']); show(['l','-slt','o.7z']); os.remove('o.7z')
show(['a','-mx1','o.7z','f.txt']); show(['l','-slt','o.7z']); os.remove('o.7z')
# zip methods
for mm in ['Copy','Deflate','Deflate64','BZip2','LZMA','PPMd','BAD']:
    show(['a',f'-mm={mm}','o.zip','f.txt'])
    if os.path.exists('o.zip'): show(['l','-slt','o.zip']); os.remove('o.zip')
# 7z options
for args in [['-ms=off'],['-ms=on'],['-mhc=off'],['-mhc=on'],['-mqs=on'],['-mmt=1'],['-mmt=off'],['-md=1m'],['-mfb=64'],['-mlc=4'],['-ms=1m']]:
    show(['a']+args+['o.7z','f.txt']); 
    if os.path.exists('o.7z'): show(['l','-slt','o.7z']); os.remove('o.7z')
# tar opts? gzip mx
show(['a','-mx1','o.gz','f.txt']); show(['l','-slt','o.gz'])
PY
grep -E '^\$ 7za|Method =|Archive size|ERROR|System|exit' /tmp/log_methods.txt | head -n 250

import sys,os,shutil,zipfile,tarfile
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from probe import show
d='/tmp/tex'

z=zipfile.ZipFile('strange.zip','w')
z.writestr('../escape.txt','esc'); z.writestr('/abs.txt','abs'); z.writestr('dir/../collapse.txt','col'); z.writestr('dir/file.txt','f'); z.writestr('./dot.txt','dot'); z.writestr('a/b/c.txt','c')
z.close()
show(['l','strange.zip'])
show(['x','-y','strange.zip','-ooutx'])
for r,ds,fs in os.walk('outx'): print(r,fs)
show(['e','-y','strange.zip','-ooute'])
for r,ds,fs in os.walk('oute'): print(r,fs)
print('escape in parent?', os.path.exists('../escape.txt'), os.path.exists('escape.txt'), os.path.exists('/abs.txt'))
# duplicate basenames flatten
z=zipfile.ZipFile('dup.zip','w'); z.writestr('x/same.txt','one'); z.writestr('y/same.txt','two'); z.close()
show(['e','dup.zip','-ooutdup'],inp='A\n')
show(['e','-y','dup.zip','-ooutdup2'])
print(os.listdir('outdup') if os.path.exists('outdup') else None, open('outdup/same.txt').read() if os.path.exists('outdup/same.txt') else '')
# spe
z=zipfile.ZipFile('root.zip','w'); z.writestr('root/file.txt','x'); z.writestr('root/sub/f2.txt','y'); z.close()
show(['x','-spe','-y','root.zip','-ooutroot']); 
for r,ds,fs in os.walk('outroot'): print(r,fs)
show(['x','-y','root.zip','-ooutroot2','root/file.txt'])
for r,ds,fs in os.walk('outroot2'): print(r,fs)
# filter patterns
for pat in ['file.txt','root/*','*.txt','*/*.txt','root','ROOT/FILE.TXT','sub/f2.txt','f2.txt']:
    show(['l','root.zip',pat])
# tar with symlink/hardlink
with tarfile.open('links.tar','w') as t:
    ti=tarfile.TarInfo('sym'); ti.type=tarfile.SYMTYPE; ti.linkname='target.txt'; ti.mtime=1000000000; t.addfile(ti)
    ti=tarfile.TarInfo('hard'); ti.type=tarfile.LNKTYPE; ti.linkname='target.txt'; ti.mtime=1000000000; t.addfile(ti)
    import io
    data=b'targetdata'; ti=tarfile.TarInfo('target.txt'); ti.size=len(data); ti.mtime=1000000000; t.addfile(ti,io.BytesIO(data))
show(['l','links.tar']); show(['l','-slt','links.tar'])
show(['x','-y','links.tar','-ooutlinks'])
for r,ds,fs in os.walk('outlinks'): print(r,fs,[(f,os.readlink(os.path.join(r,f)) if os.path.islink(os.path.join(r,f)) else '') for f in fs])
print('hard inode same?', os.stat('outlinks/hard').st_ino==os.stat('outlinks/target.txt').st_ino if os.path.exists('outlinks/hard') else None)

{"command":"cat >> src/fmt7z.py << 'PY'

# ================= WRITER =================
class WItem:
    def __init__(self,path,is_dir=False,size=0,mtime_ns=None,attr=None,data=b'',anti=False,crc=None):
        self.path=path; self.is_dir=is_dir; self.size=size; self.mtime_ns=mtime_ns; self.attr=attr; self.data=data; self.anti=anti; self.crc=crc
class WBlock:
    # either new_items with data, or preserved folder info
    def __init__(self):
        self.items=[]  # WItems that are in block (stream files)
        self.preserved_folder=None
        self.preserved_packed=[]  # list bytes
        self.pack_sizes=[]; self.packed_data=b''
        self.coders_stored=[]; self.unpack_sizes_stored=[]; self.bind_pairs=[]; self.packed_indices=[0]
        self.unpack_total=0

def bit_vector_bytes(flags):
    out=bytearray((len(flags)+7)//8)
    for i,f in enumerate(flags):
        if f: out[i//8] |= (1 << (7-(i%8)))
    return bytes(out)

def align_dummy(current_pos, header_len_before_payload, align):
    # return dummy property bytes (possibly empty) to make payload offset aligned.
    if (current_pos + header_len_before_payload) % align ==0:
        return b''
    for dummy_size in range(0, 300):
        size_len=len(write_varint(dummy_size))
        total_extra=1+size_len+dummy_size
        if (current_pos + total_extra + header_len_before_payload) % align==0:
            return b'\x19'+write_varint(dummy_size)+b'\x00'*dummy_size
    return b''

def encode_coder(coder_name, data, comp):
    name=coder_name
    if name=='Copy':
        return data, b'\x00', b'', data
    if name=='LZMA2':
        req=comp.get('dict_size') or (1<<25)
        # reduce
        ds=calc_reduced_dict(req, len(data)) if comp.get('reduce_dict',True) else req
        prop=lzma2_prop_from_dict(ds)
        ds=lzma2_dict_from_prop(prop)
        c=dict(comp); c['dict_size']=ds
        out=compress_lzma2(data,c)
        return out, b'\x21', bytes([prop]), out
    if name=='LZMA':
        req=comp.get('dict_size') or (1<<25)
        ds=calc_reduced_dict(req, len(data)) if comp.get('reduce_dict',True) else req
        prop_for_ds=lzma2_prop_from_dict(ds); ds=lzma2_dict_from_prop(prop_for_ds)
        lc=comp.get('lc',3); lp=comp.get('lp',0); pb=comp.get('pb',2)
        props=bytes([(pb*5+lp)*9+lc]) + struct.pack('<I',ds)
        filt={'id':lzma.FILTER_LZMA1,'dict_size':ds,'lc':lc,'lp':lp,'pb':pb}
        if comp.get('algo_fast'): filt['mode']=lzma.MODE_FAST
        else: filt['mode']=lzma.MODE_NORMAL
        if comp.get('nice_len'): filt['nice_len']=comp['nice_len']
        if comp.get('mf'): filt['mf']=comp['mf']
        out=lzma.compress(data,format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW,filters=[filt])
        return out, b'\x03\x01\x01', props, out
    if name=='BZip2':
        lvl=comp.get('bzip_level',9)
        out=bz2.compress(data,compresslevel=max(1,min(9,lvl)))
        # 7z BZip2 props: maybe one byte block size multiplier? In generated archives inspect coder props; decoder ignores
        # Original coder props for BZip2 in 7z: 1 byte = block size /100k -1? We'll set from level: use props observed later
        props=bytes([comp.get('bzip_block100k',9)-1]) if False else comp.get('bzip_props',b'')
        # Actually parse original: we'll be overridden by write logic using comp props if set.
        return out, b'\x04\x02\x02', props, out
    if name=='Deflate' or name=='Deflate64':
        from deflate import deflate_encode
        lvl=comp.get('deflate_level',6)
        out=deflate_encode(data, level=lvl, deflate64=(name=='Deflate64'))
        cid=b'\x04\x01\x08' if name=='Deflate' else b'\x04\x01\x09'
        return out,cid,b'',out
    if name=='Delta':
        delta=comp.get('delta',1)
        hist=[0]*delta; pos=0; out=bytearray()
        for b in data:
            out.append((b-hist[pos])&0xFF); hist[pos]=b; pos=(pos+1)%delta
        return bytes(out),b'\x03',bytes([delta-1]),bytes(out)
    if name=='BCJ':
        from filters import bcj_x86_encode
        out=bcj_x86_encode(data,0)
        return out,b'\x03\x03\x01\x03',b'',out
    if name in ('PPC','IA64','ARM','ARMT','SPARC','ARM64','RISCV'):
        # filters acting as identity for most data would be wrong for code; use liblzma via combined? For now identity (still losslessly decodable by our decoder using filter may transform back incorrectly in original)
        # To remain compatible with original decoder, better raise not-implemented at command layer for these explicit filters.
        raise DataErrorItem('E_NOTIMPL')
    if name=='Swap2':
        out=bytearray(data)
        for i in range(0,len(out)-1,2): out[i],out[i+1]=out[i+1],out[i]
        return bytes(out),b'\x02\x03\x02',b'',bytes(out)
    if name=='Swap4':
        out=bytearray(data)
        for i in range(0,len(out)-3,4): out[i],out[i+1],out[i+2],out[i+3]=out[i+3],out[i+2],out[i+1],out[i]
        return bytes(out),b'\x02\x03\x04',b'',bytes(out)
    if name=='PPMD':
        from ppmd import ppmd_encode
        out,props=ppmd_encode(data, comp)
        return out,b'\x03\x04\x01',props,out
    raise DataErrorItem('E_NOTIMPL')

def encode_block_new(block, comp):
    # comp: dict with 'coders' encoding order list names, 'password' optional, params
    data=b''.join(it.data for it in block.items)
    block.unpack_total=len(data)
    coders_enc=list(comp.get('coders') or ['LZMA2'])
    # mx0 => Copy
    stages=[]  # list of (cid,props,output_bytes_of_stage_in_encoding_order)
    cur=data
    for cname in coders_enc:
        out,cid,props,_=encode_coder(cname,cur,comp)
        stages.append((cid,props,out)); cur=out
    if comp.get('password'):
        # 7zAES encode final
        iv=os.urandom(16)
        props=bytes([0x53,0x0F])+iv
        key=derive_7zaes_key(comp['password'],b'',19)
        padded=cur + b'\x00'*(((len(cur)+15)//16)*16-len(cur))
        enc=util.aes_cbc_encrypt(key,iv,padded)
        stages.append((b'\x06\xf1\x07\x01',props,enc)); cur=enc
    block.packed_data=cur
    block.pack_sizes=[len(cur)]
    # stored order reversed stages
    stored=list(reversed(stages))
    block.coders_stored=[{'id':cid,'num_in':1,'num_out':1,'props':props} for cid,props,_ in stored]
    # unpack sizes in stored order: output size of each decoder stage.
    # Dec stage0 (stored0) output = stage before last encoding output, i.e., second last encoding stage output size, or original if only one stage.
    enc_outputs=[len(s[2]) for s in stages]
    unpack_sizes=[]
    for idx in range(len(stored)):
        # stored idx corresponds encoding stage len-1-idx; its decoded output is input to that encoding stage = previous encoding output or original data length
        enc_stage=len(stages)-1-idx
        if enc_stage==0: unpack_sizes.append(len(data))
        else: unpack_sizes.append(enc_outputs[enc_stage-1])
    block.unpack_sizes_stored=unpack_sizes
    block.bind_pairs=[(i+1,i) for i in range(len(stored)-1)]
    block.packed_indices=[0]
    # crc per item
    for it in block.items:
        if it.crc is None: it.crc=zlib.crc32(it.data)&0xFFFFFFFF
    return block

def build_folder_bytes(coders, bind_pairs, packed_indices):
    out=bytearray()
    out += write_varint(len(coders))
    total_in=0; total_out=0
    for c in coders:
        nin=c.get('num_in',1); nout=c.get('num_out',1); total_in+=nin; total_out+=nout
        idb=c['id']; props=c.get('props',b'')
        b=len(idb)
        if nin!=1 or nout!=1: b|=0x40
        if props or c.get('force_props'): b|=0x20
        out.append(b); out+=idb
        if nin!=1 or nout!=1: out+=write_varint(nin)+write_varint(nout)
        if props or c.get('force_props'): out+=write_varint(len(props))+props
    for iidx,oidx in bind_pairs:
        out+=write_varint(iidx)+write_varint(oidx)
    num_packed=total_in-(total_out-1)
    if num_packed>1:
        for idx in packed_indices: out+=write_varint(idx)
    return bytes(out)

def build_streams_info(blocks, include_substreams=True, pack_pos=0):
    # blocks list of WBlock with packed etc.
    out=bytearray()
    # PackInfo
    all_pack=[]
    for bl in blocks: all_pack.extend(bl.pack_sizes)
    out.append(0x06); out+=write_varint(pack_pos); out+=write_varint(len(all_pack)); out.append(0x09)
    for sz in all_pack: out+=write_varint(sz)
    out.append(0x00)
    # UnpackInfo
    out.append(0x07); out.append(0x0B); out+=write_varint(len(blocks)); out.append(0x00)
    for bl in blocks:
        if bl.preserved_folder is not None:
            f=bl.preserved_folder
            out+=build_folder_bytes(f.coders,f.bind_pairs,f.packed_indices)
        else:
            out+=build_folder_bytes(bl.coders_stored,bl.bind_pairs,bl.packed_indices)
    out.append(0x0C)
    for bl in blocks:
        ups=bl.preserved_folder.unpack_sizes if bl.preserved_folder is not None else bl.unpack_sizes_stored
        for sz in ups: out+=write_varint(sz)
    out.append(0x00)
    # SubStreamsInfo if any blocks
    if blocks:
        out.append(0x08)
        nums=[len(bl.items) for bl in blocks]
        if any(n!=1 for n in nums):
            out.append(0x0D)
            for n in nums: out+=write_varint(n)
            out.append(0x09)
            for bl in blocks:
                for it in bl.items[:-1]: out+=write_varint(it.size)
        out.append(0x0A)
        digests=[]
        for bl in blocks:
            for it in bl.items: digests.append(it.crc if it.crc is not None else zlib.crc32(it.data)&0xFFFFFFFF)
        out+=write_crc_vector(digests)
        out.append(0x00)
    out.append(0x00)
    return bytes(out)

def build_files_info(all_items, header_offset_start):
    # header_offset_start = length of header bytes already before FilesInfo structure content following 0x01 header byte and streams etc.
    # We will build with tracking current offset assuming caller accounted: easier caller passes prefix_len_so_far (from header start to byte before 0x05?).
    # Here `header_offset_start` is offset of the 0x05 byte from header start.
    out=bytearray()
    out.append(0x05); out+=write_varint(len(all_items))
    cur=header_offset_start+len(out)
    empty_flags=[(it.is_dir or it.size==0) if not getattr(it,'is_stream_file_override',False) else False for it in all_items]
    # Determine stream items: items that are in blocks have attribute _in_block set by caller; if not set, empty if dir or size0
    empty_flags=[]
    for it in all_items:
        inblock=getattr(it,'_in_block',None)
        if inblock is None: inblock=(not it.is_dir and it.size>0)
        empty_flags.append(not inblock)
    if any(empty_flags):
        b=bit_vector_bytes(empty_flags)
        prop=b'\x0e'+write_varint(len(b))+b; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
        empty_items=[it for it,f in zip(all_items,empty_flags) if f]
        empty_file_flags=[(not it.is_dir and not it.anti) for it in empty_items]
        if any(empty_file_flags):
            b=bit_vector_bytes(empty_file_flags); prop=b'\x0f'+write_varint(len(b))+b; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
        anti_flags=[bool(it.anti) for it in empty_items]
        if any(anti_flags):
            b=bit_vector_bytes(anti_flags); prop=b'\x10'+write_varint(len(b))+b; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
    # Name
    names_blob=b''.join(it.path.replace('/','\\').encode('utf-16le')+b'\x00\x00' if False else it.path.encode('utf-16le')+b'\x00\x00' for it in all_items)
    # 7z names use backslash separator in header? File list shows '/'; stored names in header observed "sub/b.txt" utf16 bytes with '/' (0x2f). We keep '/'.
    name_size=1+len(names_blob)
    name_header_len=1+len(write_varint(name_size))+1
    dummy=align_dummy(cur, name_header_len, 16); out+=dummy; cur+=len(dummy)
    prop=b'\x11'+write_varint(name_size)+b'\x00'+names_blob; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
    # MTime if any
    if all_items and any(it.mtime_ns is not None for it in all_items):
        alldef=all(it.mtime_ns is not None for it in all_items)
        bits=b'' if alldef else bit_vector_bytes([it.mtime_ns is not None for it in all_items])
        vals=b''.join(struct.pack('<Q',util.unixns_to_ft(it.mtime_ns)) for it in all_items if it.mtime_ns is not None)
        sz=1+len(bits)+1+len(vals)
        hdr_len=1+len(write_varint(sz))+1+len(bits)+1
        dummy=align_dummy(cur,hdr_len,8); out+=dummy; cur+=len(dummy)
        prop=b'\x14'+write_varint(sz)+bytes([1 if alldef else 0])+bits+b'\x00'+vals; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
    # Attributes
    if all_items and any(it.attr is not None for it in all_items):
        alldef=all(it.attr is not None for it in all_items)
        bits=b'' if alldef else bit_vector_bytes([it.attr is not None for it in all_items])
        vals=b''.join(struct.pack('<I',it.attr) for it in all_items if it.attr is not None)
        sz=1+len(bits)+1+len(vals)
        hdr_len=1+len(write_varint(sz))+1+len(bits)+1
        dummy=align_dummy(cur,hdr_len,4); out+=dummy; cur+=len(dummy)
        prop=b'\x15'+write_varint(sz)+bytes([1 if alldef else 0])+bits+b'\x00'+vals; out+=prop; cur+=len(prop)
    out.append(0x00)
    return bytes(out)

def compress_header_lzma(raw):
    ds=calc_reduced_dict(1<<28, len(raw))

def bit_vector_bytes(flags):
    out=bytearray((len(flags)+7)//8)
    for i,f in enumerate(flags):

def align_dummy(current_pos, header_len_before_payload, align):
    # return dummy property bytes (possibly empty) to make payload offset aligned.
    if (current_pos + header_len_before_payload) % align ==0:
        return b''
    for dummy_size in range(0, 300):
        size_len=len(write_varint(dummy_size))
        total_extra=1+size_len+dummy_size
        if (current_pos + total_extra + header_len_before_payload) % align==0:
            return b'\x19'+write_varint(dummy_size)+b'\x00'*dummy_size
    return b''

def encode_block_new(block, comp):

    data=b''.join(it.data for it in block.items)
    block.unpack_total=len(data)
    coders_enc=list(comp.get('coders') or ['LZMA2'])
    # mx0 => Copy
    stages=[]  # list of (cid,props,output_bytes_of_stage_in_encoding_order)
    cur=data
    for cname in coders_enc:
        out,cid,props,_=encode_coder(cname,cur,comp)
        stages.append((cid,props,out)); cur=out
    if comp.get('password'):
        # 7zAES encode final
        iv=os.urandom(16)
        props=bytes([0x53,0x0F])+iv
        key=derive_7zaes_key(comp['password'],b'',19)
        padded=cur + b'\x00'*(((len(cur)+15)//16)*16-len(cur))
        enc=util.aes_cbc_encrypt(key,iv,padded)
        stages.append((b'\x06\xf1\x07\x01',props,enc)); cur=enc
    block.packed_data=cur
    block.pack_sizes=[len(cur)]
    # stored order reversed stages
    stored=list(reversed(stages))
    block.coders_stored=[{'id':cid,'num_in':1,'num_out':1,'props':props} for cid,props,_ in stored]
    # unpack sizes in stored order: output size of each decoder stage.
    # Dec stage0 (stored0) output = stage before last encoding output, i.e., second last encoding stage output size, or original if only one stage.
    enc_outputs=[len(s[2]) for s in stages]
    unpack_sizes=[]
    for idx in range(len(stored)):
        # stored idx corresponds encoding stage len-1-idx; its decoded output is input to that encoding stage = previous encoding output or original data length
        enc_stage=len(stages)-1-idx
        if enc_stage==0: unpack_sizes.append(len(data))
        else: unpack_sizes.append(enc_outputs[enc_stage-1])
    block.unpack_sizes_stored=unpack_sizes
    block.bind_pairs=[(i+1,i) for i in range(len(stored)-1)]
    block.packed_indices=[0]
    # crc per item
    for it in block.items:
        if it.crc is None: it.crc=zlib.crc32(it.data)&0xFFFFFFFF

def build_folder_bytes(coders, bind_pairs, packed_indices):
    out=bytearray()
    out += write_varint(len(coders))
    total_in=0; total_out=0
    for c in coders:
        nin=c.get('num_in',1); nout=c.get('num_out',1); total_in+=nin; total_out+=nout
        idb=c['id']; props=c.get('props',b'')
        b=len(idb)
        if nin!=1 or nout!=1: b|=0x40
        if props or c.get('force_props'): b|=0x20
        out.append(b); out+=idb
        if nin!=1 or nout!=1: out+=write_varint(nin)+write_varint(nout)
        if props or c.get('force_props'): out+=write_varint(len(props))+props
    for iidx,oidx in bind_pairs:
        out+=write_varint(iidx)+write_varint(oidx)
    num_packed=total_in-(total_out-1)
    if num_packed>1:
        for idx in packed_indices: out+=write_varint(idx)
    return bytes(out)

    out.append(0x06); out+=write_varint(pack_pos); out+=write_varint(len(all_pack)); out.append(0x09)
    for sz in all_pack: out+=write_varint(sz)
    out.append(0x00)
    # UnpackInfo
    out.append(0x07); out.append(0x0B); out+=write_varint(len(blocks)); out.append(0x00)
    for bl in blocks:
        if bl.preserved_folder is not None:
            f=bl.preserved_folder
            out+=build_folder_bytes(f.coders,f.bind_pairs,f.packed_indices)
        else:
            out+=build_folder_bytes(bl.coders_stored,bl.bind_pairs,bl.packed_indices)
    out.append(0x0C)
    for bl in blocks:
        ups=bl.preserved_folder.unpack_sizes if bl.preserved_folder is not None else bl.unpack_sizes_stored
        for sz in ups: out+=write_varint(sz)
    out.append(0x00)

    if blocks:
        out.append(0x08)
        nums=[len(bl.items) for bl in blocks]
        if any(n!=1 for n in nums):
            out.append(0x0D)
            for n in nums: out+=write_varint(n)
            out.append(0x09)
            for bl in blocks:
                for it in bl.items[:-1]: out+=write_varint(it.size)
        out.append(0x0A)
        digests=[]
        for bl in blocks:
            for it in bl.items: digests.append(it.crc if it.crc is not None else zlib.crc32(it.data)&0xFFFFFFFF)

        out.append(0x00)

def compress_header_lzma(raw):

    p=lzma2_prop_from_dict(ds); ds=lzma2_dict_from_prop(p)

    out=lzma.compress(raw,format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW,filters=filt)
    props=bytes([93])+struct.pack('<I',ds)

# ---------- Writers ----------
def ntfs_extra(mtime_ns):
    ft=util.unixns_to_ft(mtime_ns) if mtime_ns is not None else 0
    payload=struct.pack('<IHHQQQ',0,1,24,ft,0,0)
    return struct.pack('<HH',0x000A,len(payload))+payload

class ZipWItem:
    def __init__(self):
        self.path=''; self.is_dir=False; self.size=0; self.data=b''; self.mtime_ns=None; self.mode=0o100644; self.attr=None; self.comment=''; self.crc=None
        self.preserved=None  # dict for old entry raw
        self.is_symlink=False

def compress_for_zip(data, method_name, comp):
    # returns (method_id, packed_bytes, version_needed, method_display, flags_extra?)
    if method_name=='Store' or len(data)==0:
        return 0,data,10
    if method_name=='Deflate':
        from deflate import deflate_encode
        lvl=comp.get('zip_level',6)
        return 8,deflate_encode(data,level=lvl),20
    if method_name=='Deflate64':
        from deflate import deflate_encode
        return 9,deflate_encode(data,level=comp.get('zip_level',6),deflate64=True),21
    if method_name=='BZip2':
        return 12,bz2.compress(data,compresslevel=comp.get('bzip_level',9)),46
    if method_name=='LZMA':
        # zip LZMA header
        ds=(1<<20)
        # dict based on comp
        from fmt7z import calc_reduced_dict,lzma2_prop_from_dict,lzma2_dict_from_prop
        req=comp.get('dict_size') or (1<<25); ds=calc_reduced_dict(req,len(data)); p=lzma2_prop_from_dict(ds); ds=lzma2_dict_from_prop(p)
        props=bytes([93])+struct.pack('<I',ds)
        filt=[{'id':lzma.FILTER_LZMA1,'dict_size':ds,'lc':3,'lp':0,'pb':2,'mode':lzma.MODE_NORMAL,'mf':lzma.MF_BT4,'nice_len':comp.get('nice_len',273)}]
        raw=lzma.compress(data,format=lzma.FORMAT_RAW,filters=filt)
        return 14, struct.pack('<HH',26,5)+props+raw,63
    if method_name=='PPMd' or method_name=='PPMD':
        from ppmd import ppmd_zip_encode
        return 98,ppmd_zip_encode(data,comp),63
    if method_name=='XZ':
        return 95,lzma.compress(data,format=lzma.FORMAT_XZ,check=lzma.CHECK_CRC32),63
    if method_name=='Zstandard':
        raise DataErrorItem('E_NOTIMPL')
    return 8,zlib.compress(data)[2:-4],20

def write_zip_archive(items, comp):
    # items ZipWItem sorted by caller
    out=bytearray(); centrals=[]
    for it in items:
        offset=len(out)
        if it.preserved is not None:
            p=it.preserved
            packed=p['packed']; crc=p['crc']; size=p['size']; psize=len(packed); method=p['method']; need=p['need']; flags=p['flags']
            dost,dosd=p['dost'],p['dosd']; ext_attr=p['ext_attr']; made_by=p['made_by']; local_extra=p.get('local_extra',b''); central_extra=p.get('central_extra',b''); int_attr=p.get('int_attr',0)
            name_raw=p['raw_name']; comment_raw=p.get('raw_comment',b'')
            # if renamed, need rebuild name/extra UTF8 flag? caller can mark preserved None then.
        else:
            data=it.data; size=len(data); crc=zlib.crc32(data)&0xFFFFFFFF if not it.is_dir else 0
            if it.crc is not None: crc=it.crc
            method_name=comp.get('zip_method','Deflate')
            if it.is_dir: method_name='Store'
            method,packed,need=compress_for_zip(data,method_name,comp)
            if method_name=='Deflate' and comp.get('store_if_bigger',True) and len(packed)>=len(data) and not comp.get('force_method'):
                method,packed,need=0,data,10
            if it.is_dir: need=20
            flags=0; psize=len(packed)
            # encryption
            aes_strength=comp.get('aes_strength')
            password=comp.get('password')
            local_extra=b''; ce_aes=b''
            if password and not it.is_dir:
                flags|=1; pwb=password.encode('utf-8')
                if aes_strength:
                    actual=method; packed=winzip_aes_encrypt(packed,pwb,aes_strength); psize=len(packed)

                else:

                    if need<20: need=20

            if any(ord(ch)>127 for ch in arcname) or comp.get('cu'):

            else:

    bw=BitWriter(); n=len(data)

/**
 * \file        lzma/lzma12.h
 * \brief       LZMA1 and LZMA2 filters
 */

/*
 * Author: Lasse Collin
 *
 * This file has been put into the public domain.
 * You can do whatever you want with this file.
 *
 * See ../lzma.h for information about liblzma as a whole.
 */

#ifndef LZMA_H_INTERNAL
#	error Never include this file directly. Use <lzma.h> instead.
#endif


/**
 * \brief       LZMA1 Filter ID
 *
 * LZMA1 is the very same thing as what was called just LZMA in LZMA Utils,
 * 7-Zip, and LZMA SDK. It's called LZMA1 here to prevent developers from
 * accidentally using LZMA when they actually want LZMA2.
 *
 * LZMA1 shouldn't be used for new applications unless you _really_ know
 * what you are doing. LZMA2 is almost always a better choice.
 */
#define LZMA_FILTER_LZMA1       LZMA_VLI_C(0x4000000000000001)

/**
 * \brief       LZMA2 Filter ID
 *
 * Usually you want this instead of LZMA1. Compared to LZMA1, LZMA2 adds
 * support for LZMA_SYNC_FLUSH, uncompressed chunks (smaller expansion
 * when trying to compress uncompressible data), possibility to change
 * lc/lp/pb in the middle of encoding, and some other internal improvements.
 */
#define LZMA_FILTER_LZMA2       LZMA_VLI_C(0x21)


/**
 * \brief       Match finders
 *
 * Match finder has major effect on both speed and compression ratio.
 * Usually hash chains are faster than binary trees.
 *
 * If you will use LZMA_SYNC_FLUSH often, the hash chains may be a better
 * choice, because binary trees get much higher compression ratio penalty
 * with LZMA_SYNC_FLUSH.
 *
 * The memory usage formulas are only rough estimates, which are closest to
 * reality when dict_size is a power of two. The formulas are  more complex
 * in reality, and can also change a little between liblzma versions. Use
 * lzma_raw_encoder_memusage() to get more accurate estimate of memory usage.
 */
typedef enum {
	LZMA_MF_HC3     = 0x03,
		/**<
		 * \brief       Hash Chain with 2- and 3-byte hashing
		 *
		 * Minimum nice_len: 3
		 *
		 * Memory usage:
		 *  - dict_size <= 16 MiB: dict_size * 7.5
		 *  - dict_size > 16 MiB: dict_size * 5.5 + 64 MiB
		 */

	LZMA_MF_HC4     = 0x04,
		/**<
		 * \brief       Hash Chain with 2-, 3-, and 4-byte hashing
		 *
		 * Minimum nice_len: 4
		 *
		 * Memory usage:
		 *  - dict_size <= 32 MiB: dict_size * 7.5
		 *  - dict_size > 32 MiB: dict_size * 6.5
		 */

	LZMA_MF_BT2     = 0x12,
		/**<
		 * \brief       Binary Tree with 2-byte hashing
		 *
		 * Minimum nice_len: 2
		 *
		 * Memory usage: dict_size * 9.5
		 */

	LZMA_MF_BT3     = 0x13,
		/**<
		 * \brief       Binary Tree with 2- and 3-byte hashing
		 *
		 * Minimum nice_len: 3
		 *
		 * Memory usage:
		 *  - dict_size <= 16 MiB: dict_size * 11.5
		 *  - dict_size > 16 MiB: dict_size * 9.5 + 64 MiB
		 */

	LZMA_MF_BT4     = 0x14
		/**<
		 * \brief       Binary Tree with 2-, 3-, and 4-byte hashing
		 *
		 * Minimum nice_len: 4
		 *
		 * Memory usage:
		 *  - dict_size <= 32 MiB: dict_size * 11.5
		 *  - dict_size > 32 MiB: dict_size * 10.5
		 */
} lzma_match_finder;


/**
 * \brief       Test if given match finder is supported
 *
 * Return true if the given match finder is supported by this liblzma build.
 * Otherwise false is returned. It is safe to call this with a value that
 * isn't listed in lzma_match_finder enumeration; the return value will be
 * false.
 *
 * There is no way to list which match finders are available in this
 * particular liblzma version and build. It would be useless, because
 * a new match finder, which the application developer wasn't aware,
 * could require giving additional options to the encoder that the older
 * match finders don't need.
 */
extern LZMA_API(lzma_bool) lzma_mf_is_supported(lzma_match_finder match_finder)
		lzma_nothrow lzma_attr_const;


/**
 * \brief       Compression modes
 *
 * This selects the function used to analyze the data produced by the match
 * finder.
 */
typedef enum {
	LZMA_MODE_FAST = 1,
		/**<
		 * \brief       Fast compression
		 *
		 * Fast mode is usually at its best when combined with
		 * a hash chain match finder.
		 */

	LZMA_MODE_NORMAL = 2
		/**<
		 * \brief       Normal compression
		 *
		 * This is usually notably slower than fast mode. Use this
		 * together with binary tree match finders to expose the
		 * full potential of the LZMA1 or LZMA2 encoder.
		 */
} lzma_mode;


/**
 * \brief       Test if given compression mode is supported
 *
 * Return true if the given compression mode is supported by this liblzma
 * build. Otherwise false is returned. It is safe to call this with a value
 * that isn't listed in lzma_mode enumeration; the return value will be false.
 *
 * There is no way to list which modes are available in this particular
 * liblzma version and build. It would be useless, because a new compression
 * mode, which the application developer wasn't aware, could require giving
 * additional options to the encoder that the older modes don't need.
 */
extern LZMA_API(lzma_bool) lzma_mode_is_supported(lzma_mode mode)
		lzma_nothrow lzma_attr_const;


/**
 * \brief       Options specific to the LZMA1 and LZMA2 filters
 *
 * Since LZMA1 and LZMA2 share most of the code, it's simplest to share
 * the options structure too. For encoding, all but the reserved variables
 * need to be initialized unless specifically mentioned otherwise.
 * lzma_lzma_preset() can be used to get a good starting point.
 *
 * For raw decoding, both LZMA1 and LZMA2 need dict_size, preset_dict, and
 * preset_dict_size (if preset_dict != NULL). LZMA1 needs also lc, lp, and pb.
 */
typedef struct {
	/**
	 * \brief       Dictionary size in bytes
	 *
	 * Dictionary size indicates how many bytes of the recently processed
	 * uncompressed data is kept in memory. One method to reduce size of
	 * the uncompressed data is to store distance-length pairs, which
	 * indicate what data to repeat from the dictionary buffer. Thus,
	 * the bigger the dictionary, the better the compression ratio
	 * usually is.
	 *
	 * Maximum size of the dictionary depends on multiple things:
	 *  - Memory usage limit
	 *  - Available address space (not a problem on 64-bit systems)
	 *  - Selected match finder (encoder only)
	 *
	 * Currently the maximum dictionary size for encoding is 1.5 GiB
	 * (i.e. (UINT32_C(1) << 30) + (UINT32_C(1) << 29)) even on 64-bit
	 * systems for certain match finder implementation reasons. In the
	 * future, there may be match finders that support bigger
	 * dictionaries.
	 *
	 * Decoder already supports dictionaries up to 4 GiB - 1 B (i.e.
	 * UINT32_MAX), so increasing the maximum dictionary size of the
	 * encoder won't cause problems for old decoders.
	 *
	 * Because extremely small dictionaries sizes would have unneeded
	 * overhead in the decoder, the minimum dictionary size is 4096 bytes.
	 *
	 * \note        When decoding, too big dictionary does no other harm
	 *              than wasting memory.
	 */
	uint32_t dict_size;
#	define LZMA_DICT_SIZE_MIN       UINT32_C(4096)
#	define LZMA_DICT_SIZE_DEFAULT   (UINT32_C(1) << 23)

	/**
	 * \brief       Pointer to an initial dictionary
	 *
	 * It is possible to initialize the LZ77 history window using
	 * a preset dictionary. It is useful when compressing many
	 * similar, relatively small chunks of data independently from
	 * each other. The preset dictionary should contain typical
	 * strings that occur in the files being compressed. The most
	 * probable strings should be near the end of the preset dictionary.
	 *
	 * This feature should be used only in special situations. For
	 * now, it works correctly only with raw encoding and decoding.
	 * Currently none of the container formats supported by
	 * liblzma allow preset dictionary when decoding, thus if
	 * you create a .xz or .lzma file with preset dictionary, it
	 * cannot be decoded with the regular decoder functions. In the
	 * future, the .xz format will likely get support for preset
	 * dictionary though.
	 */
	const uint8_t *preset_dict;

	/**
	 * \brief       Size of the preset dictionary
	 *
	 * Specifies the size of the preset dictionary. If the size is
	 * bigger than dict_size, only the last dict_size bytes are
	 * processed.
	 *
	 * This variable is read only when preset_dict is not NULL.
	 * If preset_dict is not NULL but preset_dict_size is zero,
	 * no preset dictionary is used (identical to only setting
	 * preset_dict to NULL).
	 */
	uint32_t preset_dict_size;

	/**
	 * \brief       Number of literal context bits
	 *
	 * How many of the highest bits of the previous uncompressed
	 * eight-bit byte (also known as `literal') are taken into
	 * account when predicting the bits of the next literal.
	 *
	 * E.g. in typical English text, an upper-case letter is
	 * often followed by a lower-case letter, and a lower-case
	 * letter is usually followed by another lower-case letter.
	 * In the US-ASCII character set, the highest three bits are 010
	 * for upper-case letters and 011 for lower-case letters.
	 * When lc is at least 3, the literal coding can take advantage of
	 * this property in the uncompressed data.
	 *
	 * There is a limit that applies to literal context bits and literal
	 * position bits together: lc + lp <= 4. Without this limit the
	 * decoding could become very slow, which could have security related
	 * results in some cases like email servers doing virus scanning.
	 * This limit also simplifies the internal implementation in liblzma.
	 *
	 * There may be LZMA1 streams that have lc + lp > 4 (maximum possible
	 * lc would be 8). It is not possible to decode such streams with
	 * liblzma.
	 */

def process_hash_archive_test(archive,specs,opts,is_test,flat,cand,res):
    # Special Hash format behavior
    if not is_test:
        # Extract gives Can't open as archive after header
        STREAMS.out("\n\nCan't open as archive: 1\nFiles: 0\nSize:       0\nCompressed: 0\n")
        STREAMS.err(f"ERROR: {cand.display}\nCannot open the file as archive\n\nE_NOTIMPL : Not implemented\n")
        # To signal fatal upstream, return res with errors=1 but caller will count as archive with errors and print duplicate summary in single mode. We need caller special: mark res special via exception-like attribute and set opts flag to suppress subsequent.
        # Our caller process_archive_extract is only called from do_extract_test which expects (res,errors,warnings) and will count arch_with_errors and no extra single summary because process functions normally print summary inside. Here we already printed the Can't open summary; returning errors=1 will also make caller set any_fatal. It won't print extra. Good.
        res.files=0; res.size=0; res.compressed=0
        return res,1,0
    STREAMS.out("\n")
    errors=0; total=0; files=0
    hash_sums=None; hash_name_sums=None
    if getattr(opts,'hash_specified',False):
        hash_sums={m:util.DigestSum(m) for m in opts.hash_methods}; hash_name_sums={m:util.DigestSum(m) for m in opts.hash_methods}
    selected=[it for it in archive.items if item_selected(it,specs,opts.exclude_specs,opts)]
    if not selected:
        STREAMS.out("\nNo files to process\n")
    base_dir=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(cand.fs_path)) if cand.fs_path and cand.fs_path!='-' else os.getcwd()
    for it in selected:
        item_path=it.path
        fs_path=item_path if os.path.isabs(item_path) else os.path.join(base_dir,item_path)
        if not os.path.exists(fs_path):
            errors+=1; STREAMS.err(f"ERROR: Cannot open input file : errno=2 : No such file or directory : {fs_path}\n"); continue
        STREAMS.out(f"H {item_path}\n")
        method=it.user_data.get('hash_method')
        if method not in ('CRC32','CRC64','SHA1','SHA256','XXH64'):
            errors+=1; STREAMS.err(f"ERROR: Unsupported Method : {item_path}\n"); continue
        try:
            with open(fs_path,'rb') as f: data=f.read()
        except OSError as e:
            errors+=1; STREAMS.err(f"ERROR: Cannot open input file : {util.errno_text(e)} : {fs_path}\n"); continue
        files+=1; total+=len(data)
        h=util.Hasher(method); h.update(data)
        if h.digest_text().lower()!=it.user_data.get('checksum','').lower():
            errors+=1; STREAMS.err(f"ERROR: CRC Failed : {item_path}\n")
        if hash_sums is not None:
            for m in opts.hash_methods:
                hh=util.Hasher(m); hh.update(data); hash_sums[m].add_hasher(hh); hash_name_sums[m].add_digest_internal(combined_name_digest(m,item_path,data,False))
    res.files=files; res.size=total; res.compressed=archive.physical_size

                if res.files!=1: STREAMS.out(f"{(m+'  for data and names:') if m in ('CRC32','CRC64','XXH64') else (m+' for data and names:' if m=='SHA256' else m+'   for data and names:'):<30}{hash_name_sums[m].text()}\n")

    else:
        STREAMS.out("\n"); STREAMS.out(f"Sub items Errors: {errors}\n")
        if not getattr(opts,'_multi',False):

{"command":"cat > /tmp/mkcab.py << 'PY'
import struct,zlib,os
os.makedirs('/tmp/tcab',exist_ok=True)
# two files in one folder, type MSZIP, data blocks max 32768 unpack each. File2 crosses?
files=[('hello.txt',b'hello cab world\n'*10,0x5621,0x4000,0x20),('second.bin',bytes(range(256))*4,0x5621,0x4000,0x20)]
folder_data=b''.join(x[1] for x in files)
# Make one MSZIP block with full folder data (<=32768)
comp=zlib.compressobj(6,zlib.DEFLATED,-15); cdata=b'CK'+comp.compress(folder_data)+comp.flush()
cfdata=struct.pack('<IHH',0,len(cdata),len(folder_data))+cdata
# offsets: header36 + folder8=44 coffFiles
coffFiles=44
cfile_bytes=b''; off=0
for name,data,dd,dt,at in files:
    cfile_bytes+=struct.pack('<IIHHHH',len(data),off,0,dd,dt,at)+name.encode()+b'\x00'; off+=len(data)
coffCabStart=coffFiles+len(cfile_bytes)
header=struct.pack('<4sIIIIIBBHHHHH',b'MSCF',0,0,0,coffFiles,0,3,1,1,len(files),0,0,0)
# struct above maybe mismatch - construct manually
header=b'MSCF'+struct.pack('<I',0)
total=36+8+len(cfile_bytes)+len(cfdata)
header+=struct.pack('<I',total)+struct.pack('<I',0)+struct.pack('<I',coffFiles)+struct.pack('<I',0)+bytes([3,1])+struct.pack('<HHHHH',1,len(files),0,0,0)
assert len(header)==36
folder=struct.pack('<IHH',coffCabStart,1,1)
open('/tmp/tcab/test.cab','wb').write(header+folder+cfile_bytes+cfdata)
# stored cab
cdata2=folder_data; cfdata2=struct.pack('<IHH',0,len(cdata2),len(cdata2))+cdata2; total2=36+8+len(cfile_bytes)+len(cfdata2)
header2=b'MSCF'+struct.pack('<I',0)+struct.pack('<I',total2)+struct.pack('<I',0)+struct.pack('<I',coffFiles)+struct.pack('<I',0)+bytes([3,1])+struct.pack('<HHHHH',1,len(files),0,0,0)
folder2=struct.pack('<IHH',coffCabStart,1,0)
open('/tmp/tcab/stored.cab','wb').write(header2+folder2+cfile_bytes+cfdata2)
print(total,total2)

python3 /tmp/mkcab.py && for f in /tmp/tcab/test.cab /tmp/tcab/stored.cab; do echo ===$f; /workspace/executable l $f; /workspace/executable l -slt $f; /workspace/executable t $f; done"}

import ctypes, struct

def _lib():
    lib=ctypes.CDLL('libarchive.so.13')
    lib.archive_read_new.restype=ctypes.c_void_p
    lib.archive_write_new.restype=ctypes.c_void_p
    lib.archive_entry_new.restype=ctypes.c_void_p
    lib.archive_entry_pathname.restype=ctypes.c_char_p
    lib.archive_error_string.restype=ctypes.c_char_p
    return lib

def extract_archive_entry(data, index=0):
    lib=_lib(); a=lib.archive_read_new()
    lib.archive_read_support_format_all(ctypes.c_void_p(a)); lib.archive_read_support_filter_all(ctypes.c_void_p(a))
    r=lib.archive_read_open_memory(ctypes.c_void_p(a),data,len(data))
    if r!=0: raise RuntimeError('libarchive open failed')
    result=None
    cur=0
    while True:
        entry=ctypes.c_void_p(); r=lib.archive_read_next_header(ctypes.c_void_p(a),ctypes.byref(entry))
        if r==1: break
        if r<0: raise RuntimeError('libarchive read header failed')
        size=lib.archive_entry_size(ctypes.c_void_p(entry)) if hasattr(lib,'archive_entry_size') else 0
        if cur==index:
            out=bytearray(); buf=ctypes.create_string_buffer(65536)
            while True:
                n=lib.archive_read_data(ctypes.c_void_p(a),buf,65536)
                if n==0: break
                if n<0: break
                out+=buf.raw[:n]
            result=bytes(out); break
        else:
            # skip data
            if hasattr(lib,'archive_read_data_skip'):
                lib.archive_read_data_skip(ctypes.c_void_p(a))
            else:
                buf=ctypes.create_string_buffer(65536)
                while lib.archive_read_data(ctypes.c_void_p(a),buf,65536)>0: pass
        cur+=1
    lib.archive_read_free(ctypes.c_void_p(a))
    if result is None: raise RuntimeError('entry not found')
    return result

def ppmd_decode(data,props,out_size):
    # Build a minimal single-folder 7z archive carrying this PPMD stream and let libarchive decode the PPMD codec.
    import fmt7z
    w=fmt7z.WItem('f',size=out_size or 0,mtime_ns=None,attr=0x81a48020,data=b'',crc=0); w._in_block=True
    bl=fmt7z.WBlock(); bl.items=[w]
    folder=fmt7z.Folder(); folder.coders=[{'id':b'\x03\x04\x01','num_in':1,'num_out':1,'props':props}]; folder.unpack_sizes=[out_size or 0]; folder.bind_pairs=[]; folder.packed_indices=[0]; folder.total_in=1; folder.total_out=1
    bl.preserved_folder=folder; bl.packed_data=data; bl.pack_sizes=[len(data)]; bl.unpack_total=out_size or 0
    arc=fmt7z.write_7z_archive([w],[bl],{'header_compression':False})
    out=extract_archive_entry(arc,0)
    return out[:out_size] if out_size else out

def _calc_ppmd_order_mem(comp, data_len):
    level=comp.get('level',5) if comp else 5
    order=comp.get('ppmd_order') if comp else None
    if order is None:
        order={1:4,2:4,3:5,4:5,5:6,6:8,7:16,8:24,9:32}.get(level,6)
    mem_req=None
    if comp and comp.get('ppmd_mem') is not None:
        mem_req=_parse_mem(comp.get('ppmd_mem'))
    if mem_req is None:
        maxexp={1:20,2:21,3:22,4:23,5:24,6:25,7:26,8:26,9:26}.get(level,24); mem_req=1<<maxexp
    # reduced based on data: next pow2 >= 16*size, min 65536
    need=65536
    if data_len:
        v=data_len*16; need=1
        while need<v: need <<=1
        if need<65536: need=65536
    mem=min(mem_req,need)
    if mem<65536: mem=mem_req
    return int(order),int(mem)

def _parse_mem(v):
    if isinstance(v,int): return v
    s=str(v).strip().lower()
    if s.endswith('b'): return int(s[:-1])
    if s.endswith('k'): return int(s[:-1])*1024
    if s.endswith('m'): return int(s[:-1])*1024*1024
    if s.endswith('g'): return int(s[:-1])*1024**3
    n=int(s)
    return (1<<n) if n<=31 else n

def ppmd_encode(data,comp):
    lib=_lib(); a=lib.archive_write_new(); lib.archive_write_set_format_7zip(ctypes.c_void_p(a)); lib.archive_write_set_options(ctypes.c_void_p(a),b'compression=ppmd')
    outbuf=ctypes.create_string_buffer(max(100000,len(data)*2+10000)); used=ctypes.c_size_t(0)
    lib.archive_write_open_memory(ctypes.c_void_p(a),outbuf,len(outbuf),ctypes.byref(used))
    e=lib.archive_entry_new(); lib.archive_entry_set_pathname(ctypes.c_void_p(e),b'f'); lib.archive_entry_set_size(ctypes.c_void_p(e),len(data)); lib.archive_entry_set_filetype(ctypes.c_void_p(e),0o100000); lib.archive_entry_set_perm(ctypes.c_void_p(e),0o644)
    lib.archive_write_header(ctypes.c_void_p(a),ctypes.c_void_p(e)); 
    if data: lib.archive_write_data(ctypes.c_void_p(a),data,len(data))
    lib.archive_write_close(ctypes.c_void_p(a)); lib.archive_write_free(ctypes.c_void_p(a)); lib.archive_entry_free(ctypes.c_void_p(e))
    arcbytes=outbuf.raw[:used.value]
    # Parse generated archive to extract raw PPMD stream and actual props
    import fmt7z
    arc=fmt7z.open_7z(arcbytes,'x',{})
    si=arc._si; packed=arcbytes[32+si.pack_pos:32+si.pack_pos+si.pack_sizes[0]]
    actual_props=si.folders[0].coders[0]['props']
    order_desired,mem_desired=_calc_ppmd_order_mem(comp,len(data))
    actual_order=actual_props[0] if actual_props else 6
    # The generated stream was produced with actual_order. If desired order differs, keeping actual props preserves decodability.
    # For the common defaults (and when desired == actual), replace memory with the reduced value 7-Zip would store.
    props=bytes([actual_order])+struct.pack('<I',mem_desired)
    return packed,props

def ppmd_zip_decode(packed,out_size=None):
    raise RuntimeError('PPMD ZIP decode via archive')
def ppmd_zip_encode(data,comp):
    packed,props=ppmd_encode(data,comp)
    # ZIP PPMD 2-byte properties. We use the value that 7-Zip writes by default for a PPMD stream (0x0007).
    # The underlying PPMD variant-H stream is the same as in 7z after this header.
    return b'\x07\x00'+packed

import zipfile,tarfile,gzip,bz2,lzma,os
z=zipfile.ZipFile('pyzip64.zip','w',zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,allowZip64=True)
info=zipfile.ZipInfo('a.txt'); info.file_size=5; z.writestr(info,b'12345'); z.close()
# force zip64 by setting version? zipfile adds zip64 extra only when needed, not tested here
for fmt,name in [(tarfile.PAX_FORMAT,'pypax.tar'),(tarfile.GNU_FORMAT,'pygnu.tar'),(tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT,'pyustar.tar')]:
 with tarfile.open(name,'w',format=fmt) as t: t.add('src/a.txt','a.txt'); t.add('src/sub/b.bin','sub/b.bin')
with gzip.open('py.gz','wb') as f:f.write(b'hello foreign\n')
with bz2.open('py.bz2','wb') as f:f.write(b'hello foreign\n')
with lzma.open('py.xz','wb') as f:f.write(b'hello foreign\n')
with lzma.open('py.lzma','wb',format=lzma.FORMAT_ALONE) as f:f.write(b'hello foreign\n')
PY
for f in py*.tar py*; do echo ===$f; /workspace/executable l -slt $f 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Device|Created|Accessed|Characteristics' | head -12; done; for f in pyzip.zip pyzip64.zip py*.tar py.gz py.bz2 py.xz py.lzma; do echo ===$f; diff <(/workspace/executable l -slt $f 2>&1) <(/tmp/my7za l -slt $f 2>&1) || true; diff <(/workspace/executable t $f 2>&1) <(/tmp/my7za t $f 2>&1) || true; done"}

import bz2,sys
class BR:
 def __init__(self,d):self.d=d;self.pos=0;self.buf=0;self.cnt=0
 def bit(self):
  if self.cnt==0:self.buf=self.d[self.pos];self.pos+=1;self.cnt=8
  v=(self.buf>>7)&1;self.buf=(self.buf<<1)&255;self.cnt-=1;return v
 def bits(self,n):
  v=0
  for i in range(n):v=(v<<1)|self.bit()
  return v
def build(lengths):
 maxb=max(lengths); table={}
 code=0; counts=[0]*(maxb+1)
 for l in lengths:
  if l:counts[l]+=1
 next=[0]*(maxb+1)
 for b in range(1,maxb+1):code=(code+counts[b-1])<<1;next[b]=code
 for s,l in enumerate(lengths):
  if l:table[(l,next[l])]=s;next[l]+=1
 return table,maxb
def dec(br,t):
 tab,maxb=t;code=0
 for l in range(1,maxb+1):
  code=(code<<1)|br.bit()
  if (l,code) in tab:return tab[(l,code)]
 raise Exception('bad')
def dump(data):
 br=BR(data); print('hdr',bytes([br.bits(8) for _ in range(4)]))
 while True:
  magic=br.bits(48);print('magic',hex(magic))
  if magic==0x177245385090: print('eos crc',hex(br.bits(32)));break
  print('block crc',hex(br.bits(32)),'rand',br.bit(),'origptr',br.bits(24))
  used16=[br.bit() for _ in range(16)]; used=[]
  for i,b in enumerate(used16):
   if b:
    sub=[br.bit() for _ in range(16)]; used.extend([i*16+j for j,x in enumerate(sub) if x])
  print('used chars',used)
  ngroups=br.bits(3); nselect=br.bits(15); print('groups',ngroups,'selectors',nselect)
  # selectors unary MTF
  sels=[]
  for i in range(nselect):
   c=0
   while br.bit():c+=1
   sels.append(c)
  print('selector mtf vals',sels)
  tables=[]
  alpha=len(used)+2
  for g in range(ngroups):
   lens=[]; cur=br.bits(5)
   for i in range(alpha):
    while True:
     if br.bit()==0:break
     if br.bit()==0:cur+=1
     else:cur-=1
    lens.append(cur)
   tables.append(lens);print('table',g,lens)
  # selectors MTF decode
  mtf=list(range(ngroups)); seldec=[]
  for s in sels:
   v=mtf[s];seldec.append(v);mtf.pop(s);mtf.insert(0,v)
  print('selectors decoded',seldec)
  # symbols: need decode until EOB len(used)+1, group 50
  syms=[];gpos=0;selidx=0; table=build(tables[seldec[0]])
  while True:
   if gpos==50:gpos=0;selidx+=1;table=build(tables[seldec[selidx]])
   s=dec(br,table);gpos+=1
   if s==alpha-1:break
   syms.append(s)
  print('symbols count',len(syms),syms[:100])
